e-8050.knowledge_point: Using Row Operations to Create a Column of Zeros in a 3x3 Matrix
e-8050.problem:
$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & -7 \\ 2 & 2 & -8 \\ -3 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

By applying elementary row operations of the form $R_i:=R_i+kR_1,$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary row operations?
e-8050.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make the entries below $a_{11}={\color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{1}}$ equal to ${\color{red}0}.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & -7 \\ 2 & 2 & -8 \\ -3 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & -7 \\ 0 & -6 & 6 \\ -3 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+3{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & -7 \\ 0 & -6 & 6 \\ 0 & 10 & -20\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the elementary row operations are

$\qquad$ $R_2:=R_2-2R_1\quad$ and $\quad R_3:=R_3+3R_1.$

e-8048.knowledge_point: Using Row Operations to Create a Column of Zeros in a 4x4 Matrix
e-8048.problem:
$$
[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 1 & 5 \\ 1 & 1 & 2 & -1 \\ -1 & 3 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -2 & 1 & 5\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $B$ above. By applying three matrix elementary row operations 

- $R_1 := \ldots$

- $R_3:=R_3-3R_2$

- $R_4:= \ldots$

each of the form $R_i:=R_i+kR_2,$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the missing elementary row operations?
e-8048.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries above and below $a_{22}={\color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{1}}$ equal to ${\color{red}0}.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 1 & 5 \\ 1 & 1 & 2 & -1 \\ -1 & 3 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -2 & 1 & 5\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-2{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 & -3 & 7 \\ 1 & 1 & 2 & -1 \\ -1 & 3 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -2 & 1 & 5\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-3{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 & -3 & 7 \\ 1 & 1 & 2 & -1 \\ -4 & 0 & -5 & 4 \\ 0 & -2 & 1 & 5\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+2{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 & -3 & 7 \\ 1 & 1 & 2 & -1 \\ -4 & 0 & -5 & 4 \\ 2 & 0 & 5 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the missing elementary row operations are

$\qquad$ $R_1 := R_1 - 2R_2\quad$ and $\quad R_4:=R_4+2R_2.$

e-8051.knowledge_point: Using Column Operations to Create a Row of Zeros in a 3x3 Matrix
e-8051.problem:
$$
[\begin{aligned}-6 & -5 & 1 \\ 8 & 3 & -4 \\ 9 & 7 & -2\end{aligned}]
$$

By applying elementary column operations of the form $C_i:=C_i+kC_3,$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary column operations?
e-8051.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries to the left of $a_{13}={\color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{1}}$ equal to ${\color{red}0}.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary column operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-6 & -5 & 1 \\ 8 & 3 & -4 \\ 9 & 7 & -2\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}+6{C}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & -5 & 1 \\ -16 & 3 & -4 \\ -3 & 7 & -2\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{2}:={C}_{2}+5{C}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 1 \\ -16 & -17 & -4 \\ -3 & -3 & -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the elementary column operations are

$\qquad$ $C_1:=C_1+6C_3\quad$ and $\quad C_2:=C_2+5C_3.$

e-8049.knowledge_point: Using Column Operations to Create a Row of Zeros in a 4x4 Matrix
e-8049.problem:
$$
[\begin{aligned}7 & -3 & -1 & -6 \\ 7 & -2 & -2 & -4 \\ -5 & 1 & 4 & 2 \\ -8 & -3 & -6 & -4\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $B$ above. By applying three matrix elementary column operations 

- $C_1:=\ldots$

- $C_3:= C_3 - 4C_2$

- $C_4:= \ldots$

each of the form $C_i:=C_i+kC_2,$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the missing elementary column operations?
e-8049.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries to the left and to the right of $a_{32}={\color{blue}\bbox[lightgray,2pt]{1}}$ equal to ${\color{red}0}.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary column operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}7 & -3 & -1 & -6 \\ 7 & -2 & -2 & -4 \\ -5 & 1 & 4 & 2 \\ -8 & -3 & -6 & -4\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}+5{C}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-8 & -3 & -1 & -6 \\ -3 & -2 & -2 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 & 2 \\ -23 & -3 & -6 & -4\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{3}:={C}_{3}-4{C}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-8 & -3 & 11 & -6 \\ -3 & -2 & 6 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 2 \\ -23 & -3 & 6 & -4\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{4}:={C}_{4}-2{C}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-8 & -3 & 11 & 0 \\ -3 & -2 & 6 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ -23 & -3 & 6 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding elementary column operations are

$\qquad$ $C_1:=C_1+5C_2\quad$ and $\quad C_4:=C_4-2C_2.$

before.html:
Question 1
?

A=[−1162−5−3−3−6−9],B=[3−902−5−3−990]

By applying elementary row operations of the form Ri:=Ri+kR2, the matrix A can be transformed into the matrix B. What are the elementary row operations?

a
R1:=R1+2R2 and R3:=R3+3R2
b
R1:=R1+3R2 and R3:=R3−2R2
c
R1:=R1−2R2 and R3:=R3−3R2
d
R1:=R1−2R2 and R3:=R3+3R2
e
R1:=R1+2R2 and R3:=R3−3R2
Submit

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 6 \\ 2 & -5 & -3 \\ -3 & -6 & -9\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}3 & -9 & 0 \\ 2 & -5 & -3 \\ -9 & 9 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

By applying elementary row operations of the form ${R}_{i}:={R}_{i}+k{R}_{2},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary row operations?
after.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make the entries above and below ${a}_{23}=-3$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 6 \\ 2 & -5 & -3 \\ -3 & -6 & -9\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+2{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & -9 & 0 \\ 2 & -5 & -3 \\ -3 & -6 & -9\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-3{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & -9 & 0 \\ 2 & -5 & -3 \\ -9 & 9 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the elementary row operations are

$\,$ ${R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+2{R}_{2}\,$ and $\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-3{R}_{2}.$

Question 1
?

A=[−1162−5−3−3−6−9],B=[3−902−5−3−990]

By applying elementary row operations of the form Ri:=Ri+kR2, the matrix A can be transformed into the matrix B. What are the elementary row operations?

a
R1:=R1+2R2 and R3:=R3+3R2
b
R1:=R1+3R2 and R3:=R3−2R2
c
R1:=R1−2R2 and R3:=R3−3R2
d
R1:=R1−2R2 and R3:=R3+3R2
e
R1:=R1+2R2 and R3:=R3−3R2
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

To transform A into B, we need to make the entries above and below a23=−3 equal to 0.

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

A=[−1162−5−3−3−6−9]R1:=R1+2R2∼[3−902−5−3−3−6−9]R3:=R3−3R2∼[3−902−5−3−990]=B

Therefore, the elementary row operations are

R1:=R1+2R2 and R3:=R3−3R2.

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms option e: R1 + 2R2 = (3,-9,0) and R3 - 3R2 = (-9,9,0), with R2 unchanged. These are exactly the rows of B. The incorrect feedback concerns the deliberately submitted option b.

content.knowledge_point: Using Row Operations to Create a Column of Zeros in a 3x3 Matrix
content.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 6 \\ 2 & -5 & -3 \\ -3 & -6 & -9\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}3 & -9 & 0 \\ 2 & -5 & -3 \\ -9 & 9 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

By applying elementary row operations of the form ${R}_{i}:={R}_{i}+k{R}_{2},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary row operations?
content.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make the entries above and below ${a}_{23}=-3$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 6 \\ 2 & -5 & -3 \\ -3 & -6 & -9\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+2{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & -9 & 0 \\ 2 & -5 & -3 \\ -3 & -6 & -9\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-3{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & -9 & 0 \\ 2 & -5 & -3 \\ -9 & 9 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the elementary row operations are

$\,$ ${R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+2{R}_{2}\,$ and $\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-3{R}_{2}.$

Question 2
?

A=[2−413−255−89],B=[2−41−7180−13280]

By applying elementary row operations of the form Ri:=Ri+kR1, the matrix A can be transformed into the matrix B. What are the elementary row operations?

a
R2:=R2+5R1 and R3:=R3−9R1
b
R2:=R2−9R1 and R3:=R3−5R1
c
R2:=R2−5R1 and R3:=R3+9R1
d
R2:=R2+5R1 and R3:=R3+9R1
e
R2:=R2−5R1 and R3:=R3−9R1
Submit

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 1 \\ 3 & -2 & 5 \\ 5 & -8 & 9\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 1 \\ -7 & 18 & 0 \\ -13 & 28 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

By applying elementary row operations of the form ${R}_{i}:={R}_{i}+k{R}_{1},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary row operations?
after.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make the entries below ${a}_{13}=1$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 1 \\ 3 & -2 & 5 \\ 5 & -8 & 9\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-5{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 1 \\ -7 & 18 & 0 \\ 5 & -8 & 9\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-9{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 1 \\ -7 & 18 & 0 \\ -13 & 28 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the elementary row operations are

$\,$ ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-5{R}_{1}\,$ and $\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-9{R}_{1}.$

A=[2−413−255−89],B=[2−41−7180−13280]

By applying elementary row operations of the form Ri:=Ri+kR1, the matrix A can be transformed into the matrix B. What are the elementary row operations?

a
R2:=R2+5R1 and R3:=R3−9R1
b
R2:=R2−9R1 and R3:=R3−5R1
c
R2:=R2−5R1 and R3:=R3+9R1
d
R2:=R2+5R1 and R3:=R3+9R1
e
R2:=R2−5R1 and R3:=R3−9R1
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To transform A into B, we need to make the entries below a13=1 equal to 0.

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

A=[2−413−255−89]R2:=R2−5R1∼[2−41−71805−89]R3:=R3−9R1∼[2−41−7180−13280]=B

Therefore, the elementary row operations are

R2:=R2−5R1 and R3:=R3−9R1.

content.knowledge_point: Using Row Operations to Create a Column of Zeros in a 3x3 Matrix
content.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 1 \\ 3 & -2 & 5 \\ 5 & -8 & 9\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 1 \\ -7 & 18 & 0 \\ -13 & 28 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

By applying elementary row operations of the form ${R}_{i}:={R}_{i}+k{R}_{1},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary row operations?
content.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make the entries below ${a}_{13}=1$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 1 \\ 3 & -2 & 5 \\ 5 & -8 & 9\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-5{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 1 \\ -7 & 18 & 0 \\ 5 & -8 & 9\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-9{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 1 \\ -7 & 18 & 0 \\ -13 & 28 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the elementary row operations are

$\,$ ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-5{R}_{1}\,$ and $\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-9{R}_{1}.$

Question 3

A=[−32−1121012],B=[−30−510−3012]

By applying elementary row operations of the form Ri:=Ri+kR3, the matrix A can be transformed into the matrix B. What are the elementary row operations?

a
R1:=R1+2R3 and R2:=R2−2R3
b
R1:=R1+2R3 and R2:=R2+2R3
c
R1:=R1−2R3 and R2:=R2+2R3
d
R1:=R1−2R3 and R2:=R2+R3
e
R1:=R1−2R3 and R2:=R2−2R3
Submit

decision.explanation: Subtract twice row 3 from each of rows 1 and 2: (-3,2,-1) - (0,2,4) = (-3,0,-5), and (1,2,1) - (0,2,4) = (1,0,-3). Row 3 stays unchanged, producing B.

after.name: Question 3
after.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 2 & -1 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 & -5 \\ 1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

By applying elementary row operations of the form ${R}_{i}:={R}_{i}+k{R}_{3},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary row operations?
after.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make the entries above ${a}_{32}=1$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 2 & -1 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-2{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 & -5 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-2{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 & -5 \\ 1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the elementary row operations are

$\,$ ${R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-2{R}_{3}\,$ and $\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-2{R}_{3}.$

Question 3
?

A=[−32−1121012],B=[−30−510−3012]

By applying elementary row operations of the form Ri:=Ri+kR3, the matrix A can be transformed into the matrix B. What are the elementary row operations?

a
R1:=R1+2R3 and R2:=R2−2R3
b
R1:=R1+2R3 and R2:=R2+2R3
c
R1:=R1−2R3 and R2:=R2+2R3
d
R1:=R1−2R3 and R2:=R2+R3
e
R1:=R1−2R3 and R2:=R2−2R3
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

To transform A into B, we need to make the entries above a32=1 equal to 0.

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

A=[−32−1121012]R1:=R1−2R3∼[−30−5121012]R2:=R2−2R3∼[−30−510−3012]=B

Therefore, the elementary row operations are

R1:=R1−2R3 and R2:=R2−2R3.

verification.explanation: The revealed solution confirms subtracting 2R3 from both R1 and R2. Since 2R3 = (0,2,4), the resulting rows are (-3,0,-5) and (1,0,-3), exactly as in B. Thus option e is correct; the incorrect feedback refers to the deliberately submitted option a.

content.knowledge_point: Using Row Operations to Create a Column of Zeros in a 3x3 Matrix
content.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 2 & -1 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 & -5 \\ 1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

By applying elementary row operations of the form ${R}_{i}:={R}_{i}+k{R}_{3},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary row operations?
content.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make the entries above ${a}_{32}=1$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 2 & -1 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-2{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 & -5 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-2{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 & -5 \\ 1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the elementary row operations are

$\,$ ${R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-2{R}_{3}\,$ and $\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-2{R}_{3}.$

after.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & -3 \\ 2 & 5 & 8 \\ 1 & 1 & 9\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}0 & -5 & -12 \\ 0 & 3 & -10 \\ 1 & 1 & 9\end{aligned}]
$$

By applying elementary row operations of the form ${R}_{i}:={R}_{i}+k{R}_{3},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary row operations?
after.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make the entries above ${a}_{31}=1$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & -3 \\ 2 & 5 & 8 \\ 1 & 1 & 9\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & -5 & -12 \\ 2 & 5 & 8 \\ 1 & 1 & 9\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-2{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & -5 & -12 \\ 0 & 3 & -10 \\ 1 & 1 & 9\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the elementary row operations are

$\,$ ${R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-{R}_{3}\,$ and $\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-2{R}_{3}.$

Question 4
?

A=[1−4−3258119],B=[0−5−1203−10119]

By applying elementary row operations of the form Ri:=Ri+kR3, the matrix A can be transformed into the matrix B. What are the elementary row operations?

a
R1:=R1−R3 and R2:=R2−2R3
b
R1:=R1+R3 and R2:=R2+2R3
c
R1:=R1−R3 and R2:=R2+2R3
d
R1:=R1−R3 and R2:=R2−R3
e
R1:=R1+R3 and R2:=R2−2R3
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To transform A into B, we need to make the entries above a31=1 equal to 0.

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

A=[1−4−3258119]R1:=R1−R3∼[0−5−12258119]R2:=R2−2R3∼[0−5−1203−10119]=B

Therefore, the elementary row operations are

R1:=R1−R3 and R2:=R2−2R3.

content.knowledge_point: Using Row Operations to Create a Column of Zeros in a 3x3 Matrix
content.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & -3 \\ 2 & 5 & 8 \\ 1 & 1 & 9\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}0 & -5 & -12 \\ 0 & 3 & -10 \\ 1 & 1 & 9\end{aligned}]
$$

By applying elementary row operations of the form ${R}_{i}:={R}_{i}+k{R}_{3},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary row operations?
content.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make the entries above ${a}_{31}=1$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & -3 \\ 2 & 5 & 8 \\ 1 & 1 & 9\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & -5 & -12 \\ 2 & 5 & 8 \\ 1 & 1 & 9\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-2{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & -5 & -12 \\ 0 & 3 & -10 \\ 1 & 1 & 9\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the elementary row operations are

$\,$ ${R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-{R}_{3}\,$ and $\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-2{R}_{3}.$

By applying elementary row operations of the form Ri:=Ri+kR3, the matrix A can be transformed into the matrix B. What are the elementary row operations?

a
R1:=R1−2R3 and R2:=R2−3R3
b
R1:=R1−3R3 and R2:=R2+2R3
c
R1:=R1+2R3 and R2:=R2−3R3

after.name: Question 5
after.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}7 & 4 & 2 \\ -9 & -6 & -12 \\ 6 & 2 & 5\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-5 & 0 & -8 \\ 9 & 0 & 3 \\ 6 & 2 & 5\end{aligned}]
$$

By applying elementary row operations of the form ${R}_{i}:={R}_{i}+k{R}_{3},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary row operations?
after.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make the entries above ${a}_{32}=2$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}7 & 4 & 2 \\ -9 & -6 & -12 \\ 6 & 2 & 5\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-2{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-5 & 0 & -8 \\ -9 & -6 & -12 \\ 6 & 2 & 5\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+3{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-5 & 0 & -8 \\ 9 & 0 & 3 \\ 6 & 2 & 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the elementary row operations are

$\,$ ${R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-2{R}_{3}\,$ and $\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+3{R}_{3}.$

Question 5

A=[742−9−6−12625],B=[−50−8903625]

By applying elementary row operations of the form Ri:=Ri+kR3, the matrix A can be transformed into the matrix B. What are the elementary row operations?

a
R1:=R1−2R3 and R2:=R2−3R3
b
R1:=R1−3R3 and R2:=R2+2R3
c
R1:=R1+2R3 and R2:=R2−3R3
d
R1:=R1−2R3 and R2:=R2+3R3
e
R1:=R1+2R3 and R2:=R2+3R3
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To transform A into B, we need to make the entries above a32=2 equal to 0.

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

A=[742−9−6−12625]R1:=R1−2R3∼[−50−8−9−6−12625]R2:=R2+3R3∼[−50−8903625]=B

Therefore, the elementary row operations are

R1:=R1−2R3 and R2:=R2+3R3.

content.knowledge_point: Using Row Operations to Create a Column of Zeros in a 3x3 Matrix
content.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}7 & 4 & 2 \\ -9 & -6 & -12 \\ 6 & 2 & 5\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-5 & 0 & -8 \\ 9 & 0 & 3 \\ 6 & 2 & 5\end{aligned}]
$$

By applying elementary row operations of the form ${R}_{i}:={R}_{i}+k{R}_{3},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary row operations?
content.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make the entries above ${a}_{32}=2$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}7 & 4 & 2 \\ -9 & -6 & -12 \\ 6 & 2 & 5\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-2{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-5 & 0 & -8 \\ -9 & -6 & -12 \\ 6 & 2 & 5\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+3{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-5 & 0 & -8 \\ 9 & 0 & 3 \\ 6 & 2 & 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the elementary row operations are

$\,$ ${R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-2{R}_{3}\,$ and $\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+3{R}_{3}.$

To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries above and below ${a}_{22}=-1$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 3 & -4 & 5 \\ 5 & -1 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 7 & 2 \\ 0 & 5 & 4 & -3\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+3{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}13 & 0 & 5 & 5 \\ 5 & -1 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 7 & 2 \\ 0 & 5 & 4 & -3\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+4{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}13 & 0 & 5 & 5 \\ 5 & -1 & 3 & 0 \\ 20 & 0 & 19 & 2 \\ 0 & 5 & 4 & -3\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+5{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}13 & 0 & 5 & 5 \\ 5 & -1 & 3 & 0 \\ 20 & 0 & 19 & 2 \\ 25 & 0 & 19 & -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the missing elementary row operations are

$\,$ ${R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+3{R}_{2}\,$ and $\,{R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+5{R}_{2}.$

$$

after.name: Question 7
after.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 6 & 1 & 1 \\ -6 & -5 & 4 & 0 \\ -5 & 3 & 3 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 2 & 9\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 6 & 1 & 1 \\ 10 & -29 & 0 & -4 \\ 7 & -15 & 0 & -2 \\ 9 & -11 & 0 & 7\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $B$ above. By applying three matrix elementary row operations 

- ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-4{R}_{1}$
- ${R}_{3}:=…$
- ${R}_{4}:=…$

each of the form ${R}_{i}:={R}_{i}+k{R}_{1},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the missing elementary row operations?
after.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries below ${a}_{13}=1$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-4 & 6 & 1 & 1 \\ -6 & -5 & 4 & 0 \\ -5 & 3 & 3 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 2 & 9\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-4{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-4 & 6 & 1 & 1 \\ 10 & -29 & 0 & -4 \\ -5 & 3 & 3 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 2 & 9\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-3{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-4 & 6 & 1 & 1 \\ 10 & -29 & 0 & -4 \\ 7 & -15 & 0 & -2 \\ 1 & 1 & 2 & 9\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{4}:={R}_{4}-2{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-4 & 6 & 1 & 1 \\ 10 & -29 & 0 & -4 \\ 7 & -15 & 0 & -2 \\ 9 & -11 & 0 & 7\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the missing elementary row operations are

$\,$ ${R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-3{R}_{1}\,$ and $\,{R}_{4}:={R}_{4}-2{R}_{1}.$

content.knowledge_point: Using Row Operations to Create a Column of Zeros in a 4x4 Matrix
content.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 6 & 1 & 1 \\ -6 & -5 & 4 & 0 \\ -5 & 3 & 3 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 2 & 9\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 6 & 1 & 1 \\ 10 & -29 & 0 & -4 \\ 7 & -15 & 0 & -2 \\ 9 & -11 & 0 & 7\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $B$ above. By applying three matrix elementary row operations 

- ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-4{R}_{1}$
- ${R}_{3}:=…$
- ${R}_{4}:=…$

each of the form ${R}_{i}:={R}_{i}+k{R}_{1},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the missing elementary row operations?
content.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries below ${a}_{13}=1$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-4 & 6 & 1 & 1 \\ -6 & -5 & 4 & 0 \\ -5 & 3 & 3 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 2 & 9\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-4{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-4 & 6 & 1 & 1 \\ 10 & -29 & 0 & -4 \\ -5 & 3 & 3 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 2 & 9\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-3{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-4 & 6 & 1 & 1 \\ 10 & -29 & 0 & -4 \\ 7 & -15 & 0 & -2 \\ 1 & 1 & 2 & 9\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{4}:={R}_{4}-2{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-4 & 6 & 1 & 1 \\ 10 & -29 & 0 & -4 \\ 7 & -15 & 0 & -2 \\ 9 & -11 & 0 & 7\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the missing elementary row operations are

$\,$ ${R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-3{R}_{1}\,$ and $\,{R}_{4}:={R}_{4}-2{R}_{1}.$

after.name: Question 8
after.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}7 & -3 & -4 & 14 \\ 8 & 2 & -4 & 6 \\ 3 & -5 & -2 & 8 \\ 11 & -1 & 2 & 8\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-26 & 0 & -10 & -10 \\ 30 & 0 & 0 & 22 \\ -52 & 0 & -12 & -32 \\ 11 & -1 & 2 & 8\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $B$ above. By applying three matrix elementary row operations 

- ${R}_{1}:=…$
- ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{4}$
- ${R}_{3}:=…$

each of the form ${R}_{i}:={R}_{i}+k{R}_{4},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the missing elementary row operations?
after.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries above ${a}_{42}=-1$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}7 & -3 & -4 & 14 \\ 8 & 2 & -4 & 6 \\ 3 & -5 & -2 & 8 \\ 11 & -1 & 2 & 8\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-3{R}_{4}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-26 & 0 & -10 & -10 \\ 8 & 2 & -4 & 6 \\ 3 & -5 & -2 & 8 \\ 11 & -1 & 2 & 8\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{4}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-26 & 0 & -10 & -10 \\ 30 & 0 & 0 & 22 \\ 3 & -5 & -2 & 8 \\ 11 & -1 & 2 & 8\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-5{R}_{4}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-26 & 0 & -10 & -10 \\ 30 & 0 & 0 & 22 \\ -52 & 0 & -12 & -32 \\ 11 & -1 & 2 & 8\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the missing elementary row operations are

\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}7 & -3 & -4 & 14 \\ 8 & 2 & -4 & 6 \\ 3 & -5 & -2 & 8 \\ 11 & -1 & 2 & 8\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-3{R}_{4}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-26 & 0 & -10 & -10 \\ 8 & 2 & -4 & 6 \\ 3 & -5 & -2 & 8 \\ 11 & -1 & 2 & 8\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{4}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-26 & 0 & -10 & -10 \\ 30 & 0 & 0 & 22 \\ 3 & -5 & -2 & 8 \\ 11 & -1 & 2 & 8\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-5{R}_{4}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-26 & 0 & -10 & -10 \\ 30 & 0 & 0 & 22 \\ -52 & 0 & -12 & -32 \\ 11 & -1 & 2 & 8\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the missing elementary row operations are

$\,$ ${R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-3{R}_{4}\,$ and $\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-5{R}_{4}.$

A=[−1223131−2013−34−2−3−4],B=[−3−407131−2−3−803770−10]

Consider the matrices A and B above. By applying three matrix elementary row operations

  1. R1:=R1−2R2
  2. R3:=…
  3. R4:=…
each of the form Ri:=Ri+kR2, the matrix A can be transformed into the matrix B. What are the missing elementary row operations?

a

b

c
R3:=R3+3R2 and R4:=R4+3R2

after.name: Question 9
after.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 2 & 3 \\ 1 & 3 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & -3 \\ 4 & -2 & -3 & -4\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-3 & -4 & 0 & 7 \\ 1 & 3 & 1 & -2 \\ -3 & -8 & 0 & 3 \\ 7 & 7 & 0 & -10\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $B$ above. By applying three matrix elementary row operations 

- ${R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-2{R}_{2}$
- ${R}_{3}:=…$
- ${R}_{4}:=…$

each of the form ${R}_{i}:={R}_{i}+k{R}_{2},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the missing elementary row operations?
after.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries above and below ${a}_{23}=1$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 2 & 3 \\ 1 & 3 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & -3 \\ 4 & -2 & -3 & -4\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-2{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & -4 & 0 & 7 \\ 1 & 3 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & -3 \\ 4 & -2 & -3 & -4\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-3{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & -4 & 0 & 7 \\ 1 & 3 & 1 & -2 \\ -3 & -8 & 0 & 3 \\ 4 & -2 & -3 & -4\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+3{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & -4 & 0 & 7 \\ 1 & 3 & 1 & -2 \\ -3 & -8 & 0 & 3 \\ 7 & 7 & 0 & -10\end{aligned}] \\  & =B.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the missing elementary row operations are

$\,$ ${R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-3{R}_{2}\,$ and $\,{R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+3{R}_{2}.$

content.knowledge_point: Using Row Operations to Create a Column of Zeros in a 4x4 Matrix
content.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 2 & 3 \\ 1 & 3 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & -3 \\ 4 & -2 & -3 & -4\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-3 & -4 & 0 & 7 \\ 1 & 3 & 1 & -2 \\ -3 & -8 & 0 & 3 \\ 7 & 7 & 0 & -10\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $B$ above. By applying three matrix elementary row operations 

- ${R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-2{R}_{2}$
- ${R}_{3}:=…$
- ${R}_{4}:=…$

each of the form ${R}_{i}:={R}_{i}+k{R}_{2},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the missing elementary row operations?
content.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries above and below ${a}_{23}=1$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 2 & 3 \\ 1 & 3 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & -3 \\ 4 & -2 & -3 & -4\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-2{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & -4 & 0 & 7 \\ 1 & 3 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & -3 \\ 4 & -2 & -3 & -4\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-3{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & -4 & 0 & 7 \\ 1 & 3 & 1 & -2 \\ -3 & -8 & 0 & 3 \\ 4 & -2 & -3 & -4\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+3{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & -4 & 0 & 7 \\ 1 & 3 & 1 & -2 \\ -3 & -8 & 0 & 3 \\ 7 & 7 & 0 & -10\end{aligned}] \\  & =B.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the missing elementary row operations are

$\,$ ${R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-3{R}_{2}\,$ and $\,{R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+3{R}_{2}.$

after.name: Question 10
after.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 & 1 & 8 \\ 1 & 2 & 3 & -4 \\ 0 & 5 & 4 & -2 \\ 4 & -3 & -1 & -6\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 21 & 17 & 0 \\ 1 & -8 & -5 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & 4 & -2 \\ 4 & -18 & -13 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $B$ above. By applying three matrix elementary row operations 

- ${R}_{1}:=…$
- ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-2{R}_{3}$
- ${R}_{4}:=…$

each of the form ${R}_{i}:={R}_{i}+k{R}_{3},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the missing elementary row operations?
after.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries above and below ${a}_{34}=-2$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 & 1 & 8 \\ 1 & 2 & 3 & -4 \\ 0 & 5 & 4 & -2 \\ 4 & -3 & -1 & -6\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+4{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & 21 & 17 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 3 & -4 \\ 0 & 5 & 4 & -2 \\ 4 & -3 & -1 & -6\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-2{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & 21 & 17 & 0 \\ 1 & -8 & -5 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & 4 & -2 \\ 4 & -3 & -1 & -6\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{4}:={R}_{4}-3{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & 21 & 17 & 0 \\ 1 & -8 & -5 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & 4 & -2 \\ 4 & -18 & -13 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =B.\end{aligned}
$$

  

Therefore, the missing elementary row operations are

\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 & 1 & 8 \\ 1 & 2 & 3 & -4 \\ 0 & 5 & 4 & -2 \\ 4 & -3 & -1 & -6\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+4{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & 21 & 17 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 3 & -4 \\ 0 & 5 & 4 & -2 \\ 4 & -3 & -1 & -6\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-2{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & 21 & 17 & 0 \\ 1 & -8 & -5 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & 4 & -2 \\ 4 & -3 & -1 & -6\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{4}:={R}_{4}-3{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & 21 & 17 & 0 \\ 1 & -8 & -5 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & 4 & -2 \\ 4 & -18 & -13 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =B.\end{aligned}
$$

  

Therefore, the missing elementary row operations are

$\,$ ${R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+4{R}_{3}\,$ and $\,{R}_{4}:={R}_{4}-3{R}_{3}.$

Question 11
?

A=[132119047],B=[12−7100047]

By applying elementary column operations of the form Ci:=Ci+kC1, the matrix A can be transformed into the matrix B. What are the elementary column operations?

a
C2:=C2−C1 and C3:=C3+9C1
b
C2:=C2+C1 and C3:=C3−9C1
c
C2:=C2−3C1 and C3:=C3−3C1
d
C2:=C2−C1 and C3:=C3−9C1
e
C2:=C2−9C1 and C3:=C3−C1
Submit

decision.explanation: C2 - C1 = (3,1,4) - (1,1,0) = (2,0,4). C3 - 9C1 = (2,9,7) - (9,9,0) = (-7,0,7). These match the columns of B, so option d is correct.

after.name: Question 11
after.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 2 \\ 1 & 1 & 9 \\ 0 & 4 & 7\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -7 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 7\end{aligned}]
$$

By applying elementary column operations of the form ${C}_{i}:={C}_{i}+k{C}_{1},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary column operations?
after.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries to the right of ${a}_{21}=1$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary column operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 2 \\ 1 & 1 & 9 \\ 0 & 4 & 7\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{2}:={C}_{2}-{C}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 & 9 \\ 0 & 4 & 7\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{3}:={C}_{3}-9{C}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -7 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 7\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the elementary column operations are

$\,$ ${C}_{1}:={C}_{1}-{C}_{2}\,$ and $\,{C}_{3}:={C}_{3}-9{C}_{1}.$

Question 11
?

A=[132119047],B=[12−7100047]

By applying elementary column operations of the form Ci:=Ci+kC1, the matrix A can be transformed into the matrix B. What are the elementary column operations?

a
C2:=C2−C1 and C3:=C3+9C1
b
C2:=C2+C1 and C3:=C3−9C1
c
C2:=C2−3C1 and C3:=C3−3C1
d
C2:=C2−C1 and C3:=C3−9C1
e
C2:=C2−9C1 and C3:=C3−C1
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To transform A into B, we need to make entries to the right of a21=1 equal to 0.

To do this, we can apply the following elementary column operations:

A=[132119047]C2:=C2−C1∼[122109047]C3:=C3−9C1∼[12−7100047]=B

Therefore, the elementary column operations are

C1:=C1−C2 and C3:=C3−9C1.

content.knowledge_point: Using Column Operations to Create a Row of Zeros in a 3x3 Matrix
content.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 2 \\ 1 & 1 & 9 \\ 0 & 4 & 7\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -7 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 7\end{aligned}]
$$

By applying elementary column operations of the form ${C}_{i}:={C}_{i}+k{C}_{1},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary column operations?
content.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries to the right of ${a}_{21}=1$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary column operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 2 \\ 1 & 1 & 9 \\ 0 & 4 & 7\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{2}:={C}_{2}-{C}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 & 9 \\ 0 & 4 & 7\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{3}:={C}_{3}-9{C}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -7 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 7\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the elementary column operations are

$\,$ ${C}_{1}:={C}_{1}-{C}_{2}\,$ and $\,{C}_{3}:={C}_{3}-9{C}_{1}.$

Question 12
?

A=[422−671−7−52],B=[002−861−11−72]

By applying elementary column operations of the form Ci:=Ci+kC3, the matrix A can be transformed into the matrix B. What are the elementary column operations?

a
C1:=C1+2C3 and C2:=C2−C3
b
C1:=C1−2C3 and C2:=C2−C3
c
C1:=C1−6C3 and C2:=C2−C3
d
C1:=C1−C3 and C2:=C2−2C3
e
C1:=C1−2C3 and C2:=C2+C3
Submit

after.name: Question 12
after.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}4 & 2 & 2 \\ -6 & 7 & 1 \\ -7 & -5 & 2\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 2 \\ -8 & 6 & 1 \\ -11 & -7 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

By applying elementary column operations of the form ${C}_{i}:={C}_{i}+k{C}_{3},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary column operations?
after.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries to the left of ${a}_{13}=2$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary column operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 2 & 2 \\ -6 & 7 & 1 \\ -7 & -5 & 2\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}-2{C}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 & 2 \\ -8 & 7 & 1 \\ -11 & -5 & 2\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{2}:={C}_{2}-{C}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 2 \\ -8 & 6 & 1 \\ -11 & -7 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the elementary column operations are

$\,$ ${C}_{1}:={C}_{1}-2{C}_{3}\,$ and $\,{C}_{2}:={C}_{2}-{C}_{3}.$

Question 12
?

A=[422−671−7−52],B=[002−861−11−72]

By applying elementary column operations of the form Ci:=Ci+kC3, the matrix A can be transformed into the matrix B. What are the elementary column operations?

a
C1:=C1+2C3 and C2:=C2−C3
b
C1:=C1−2C3 and C2:=C2−C3
c
C1:=C1−6C3 and C2:=C2−C3
d
C1:=C1−C3 and C2:=C2−2C3
e
C1:=C1−2C3 and C2:=C2+C3
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

To transform A into B, we need to make entries to the left of a13=2 equal to 0.

To do this, we can apply the following elementary column operations:

A=[422−671−7−52]C1:=C1−2C3∼[022−871−11−52]C2:=C2−C3∼[002−861−11−72]=B

Therefore, the elementary column operations are

C1:=C1−2C3 and C2:=C2−C3.

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms option b: C1 - 2C3 = (0,-8,-11) and C2 - C3 = (0,6,-7), matching B. The incorrect feedback refers to the deliberately submitted option c.

content.knowledge_point: Using Column Operations to Create a Row of Zeros in a 3x3 Matrix
content.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}4 & 2 & 2 \\ -6 & 7 & 1 \\ -7 & -5 & 2\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 2 \\ -8 & 6 & 1 \\ -11 & -7 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

By applying elementary column operations of the form ${C}_{i}:={C}_{i}+k{C}_{3},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary column operations?
content.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries to the left of ${a}_{13}=2$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary column operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 2 & 2 \\ -6 & 7 & 1 \\ -7 & -5 & 2\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}-2{C}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 & 2 \\ -8 & 7 & 1 \\ -11 & -5 & 2\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{2}:={C}_{2}-{C}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 2 \\ -8 & 6 & 1 \\ -11 & -7 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the elementary column operations are

$\,$ ${C}_{1}:={C}_{1}-2{C}_{3}\,$ and $\,{C}_{2}:={C}_{2}-{C}_{3}.$

Question 13
?

A=[105−5−13−4880],B=[050−73−1−888]

By applying elementary column operations of the form Ci:=Ci+kC2, the matrix A can be transformed into the matrix B. What are the elementary column operations?

a
C1:=C1−C2 and C3:=C3+C2
b
C1:=C1−2C2 and C3:=C3+C2
c
C1:=C1−C2 and C3:=C3+2C2
d
C1:=C1−2C2 and C3:=C3−C2
e
C1:=C1+2C2 and C3:=C3+C2
Submit

after.name: Question 13
after.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}10 & 5 & -5 \\ -1 & 3 & -4 \\ 8 & 8 & 0\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}0 & 5 & 0 \\ -7 & 3 & -1 \\ -8 & 8 & 8\end{aligned}]
$$

By applying elementary column operations of the form ${C}_{i}:={C}_{i}+k{C}_{2},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary column operations?
after.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries to the left and to the right of ${a}_{12}=5$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary column operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}10 & 5 & -5 \\ -1 & 3 & -4 \\ 8 & 8 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}-2{C}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & 5 & -5 \\ -7 & 3 & -4 \\ -8 & 8 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{3}:={C}_{3}+{C}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & 5 & 0 \\ -7 & 3 & -1 \\ -8 & 8 & 8\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the elementary column operations are

$\,$ ${C}_{1}:={C}_{1}-2{C}_{2}\,$ and $\,{C}_{3}:={C}_{3}+{C}_{2}.$

Question 13
?

A=[105−5−13−4880],B=[050−73−1−888]

By applying elementary column operations of the form Ci:=Ci+kC2, the matrix A can be transformed into the matrix B. What are the elementary column operations?

a
C1:=C1−C2 and C3:=C3+C2
b
C1:=C1−2C2 and C3:=C3+C2
c
C1:=C1−C2 and C3:=C3+2C2
d
C1:=C1−2C2 and C3:=C3−C2
e
C1:=C1+2C2 and C3:=C3+C2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To transform A into B, we need to make entries to the left and to the right of a12=5 equal to 0.

To do this, we can apply the following elementary column operations:

A=[105−5−13−4880]C1:=C1−2C2∼[05−5−73−4−880]C3:=C3+C2∼[050−73−1−888]=B

Therefore, the elementary column operations are

C1:=C1−2C2 and C3:=C3+C2.

content.knowledge_point: Using Column Operations to Create a Row of Zeros in a 3x3 Matrix
content.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}10 & 5 & -5 \\ -1 & 3 & -4 \\ 8 & 8 & 0\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}0 & 5 & 0 \\ -7 & 3 & -1 \\ -8 & 8 & 8\end{aligned}]
$$

By applying elementary column operations of the form ${C}_{i}:={C}_{i}+k{C}_{2},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary column operations?
content.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries to the left and to the right of ${a}_{12}=5$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary column operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}10 & 5 & -5 \\ -1 & 3 & -4 \\ 8 & 8 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}-2{C}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & 5 & -5 \\ -7 & 3 & -4 \\ -8 & 8 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{3}:={C}_{3}+{C}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & 5 & 0 \\ -7 & 3 & -1 \\ -8 & 8 & 8\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the elementary column operations are

$\,$ ${C}_{1}:={C}_{1}-2{C}_{2}\,$ and $\,{C}_{3}:={C}_{3}+{C}_{2}.$

Question 14
?

A=[−122131341],B=[−7−62−2−11001]

By applying elementary column operations of the form Ci:=Ci+kC3, the matrix A can be transformed into the matrix B. What are the elementary column operations?

a
C1:=C1−4C3 and C2:=C2−3C3
b
C1:=C1−3C3 and C2:=C2+4C3
c
C1:=C1−3C3 and C2:=C2+C3
d
C1:=C1−3C3 and C2:=C2−4C3
e
C1:=C1+4C3 and C2:=C2−3C3
Submit

after.name: Question 14
after.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 2 \\ 1 & 3 & 1 \\ 3 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-7 & -6 & 2 \\ -2 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

By applying elementary column operations of the form ${C}_{i}:={C}_{i}+k{C}_{3},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary column operations?
after.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries to the left of ${a}_{33}=1$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary column operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 2 \\ 1 & 3 & 1 \\ 3 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}-3{C}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-7 & 2 & 2 \\ -2 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{2}:={C}_{2}-4{C}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-7 & -6 & 2 \\ -2 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the elementary column operations are

$\,$ ${C}_{1}:={C}_{1}-3{C}_{3}\,$ and $\,{C}_{2}:={C}_{2}-4{C}_{3}.$

By applying elementary column operations of the form Ci:=Ci+kC3, the matrix A can be transformed into the matrix B. What are the elementary column operations?

a
C1:=C1−4C3 and C2:=C2−3C3
b
C1:=C1−3C3 and C2:=C2+4C3
c
C1:=C1−3C3 and C2:=C2+C3
d
C1:=C1−3C3 and C2:=C2−4C3
e
C1:=C1+4C3 and C2:=C2−3C3
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

To transform A into B, we need to make entries to the left of a33=1 equal to 0.

To do this, we can apply the following elementary column operations:

A=[−122131341]C1:=C1−3C3∼[−722−231041]C2:=C2−4C3∼[−7−62−2−11001]=B

Therefore, the elementary column operations are

C1:=C1−3C3 and C2:=C2−4C3.

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms option d. C1 - 3C3 = (-7,-2,0) and C2 - 4C3 = (-6,-1,0), matching B with C3 unchanged. The incorrect feedback concerns the deliberately submitted option c.

content.knowledge_point: Using Column Operations to Create a Row of Zeros in a 3x3 Matrix
content.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 2 \\ 1 & 3 & 1 \\ 3 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-7 & -6 & 2 \\ -2 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

By applying elementary column operations of the form ${C}_{i}:={C}_{i}+k{C}_{3},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary column operations?
content.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries to the left of ${a}_{33}=1$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary column operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 2 \\ 1 & 3 & 1 \\ 3 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}-3{C}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-7 & 2 & 2 \\ -2 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{2}:={C}_{2}-4{C}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-7 & -6 & 2 \\ -2 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the elementary column operations are

$\,$ ${C}_{1}:={C}_{1}-3{C}_{3}\,$ and $\,{C}_{2}:={C}_{2}-4{C}_{3}.$

Question 15
?

A=[42−9154−1231−5],B=[−221348010]

By applying elementary column operations of the form Ci:=Ci+kC2, the matrix A can be transformed into the matrix B. What are the elementary column operations?

a
C1:=C1+3C2 and C3:=C3−5C2
b
C1:=C1+3C2 and C3:=C3+5C2
c
C1:=C1−5C2 and C3:=C3+3C2
d
C1:=C1−3C2 and C3:=C3−5C2
e
C1:=C1−3C2 and C3:=C3+5C2
Submit

after.name: Question 15
after.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}4 & 2 & -9 \\ 15 & 4 & -12 \\ 3 & 1 & -5\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & 1 \\ 3 & 4 & 8 \\ 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

By applying elementary column operations of the form ${C}_{i}:={C}_{i}+k{C}_{2},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary column operations?
after.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries to the left and to the right of ${a}_{32}=1$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary column operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 2 & -9 \\ 15 & 4 & -12 \\ 3 & 1 & -5\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}-3{C}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & -9 \\ 3 & 4 & -12 \\ 0 & 1 & -5\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{3}:={C}_{3}+5{C}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & 1 \\ 3 & 4 & 8 \\ 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the elementary column operations are

$\,$ ${C}_{1}:={C}_{1}-3{C}_{2}\,$ and $\,{C}_{3}:={C}_{3}+5{C}_{2}.$

Question 15
?

A=[42−9154−1231−5],B=[−221348010]

By applying elementary column operations of the form Ci:=Ci+kC2, the matrix A can be transformed into the matrix B. What are the elementary column operations?

a
C1:=C1+3C2 and C3:=C3−5C2
b
C1:=C1+3C2 and C3:=C3+5C2
c
C1:=C1−5C2 and C3:=C3+3C2
d
C1:=C1−3C2 and C3:=C3−5C2
e
C1:=C1−3C2 and C3:=C3+5C2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To transform A into B, we need to make entries to the left and to the right of a32=1 equal to 0.

To do this, we can apply the following elementary column operations:

A=[42−9154−1231−5]C1:=C1−3C2∼[−22−934−1201−5]C3:=C3+5C2∼[−221348010]=B

Therefore, the elementary column operations are

C1:=C1−3C2 and C3:=C3+5C2.

content.knowledge_point: Using Column Operations to Create a Row of Zeros in a 3x3 Matrix
content.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}4 & 2 & -9 \\ 15 & 4 & -12 \\ 3 & 1 & -5\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & 1 \\ 3 & 4 & 8 \\ 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

By applying elementary column operations of the form ${C}_{i}:={C}_{i}+k{C}_{2},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary column operations?
content.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries to the left and to the right of ${a}_{32}=1$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary column operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 2 & -9 \\ 15 & 4 & -12 \\ 3 & 1 & -5\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}-3{C}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & -9 \\ 3 & 4 & -12 \\ 0 & 1 & -5\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{3}:={C}_{3}+5{C}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & 1 \\ 3 & 4 & 8 \\ 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the elementary column operations are

$\,$ ${C}_{1}:={C}_{1}-3{C}_{2}\,$ and $\,{C}_{3}:={C}_{3}+5{C}_{2}.$

after.name: Question 16
after.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 & 2 \\ 1 & 7 & 3 & 9 \\ 2 & 3 & 0 & 1 \\ 2 & 1 & 1 & 7\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 & 2 \\ -5 & 4 & 3 & -12 \\ 2 & 3 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $B$ above. By applying three matrix elementary column operations 

- ${C}_{1}:=…$
- ${C}_{2}:={C}_{2}-{C}_{3}$
- ${C}_{4}:=…$

each of the form ${C}_{i}:={C}_{i}+k{C}_{3},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the missing elementary column operations?
after.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries to the left and to the right of ${a}_{43}=1$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary column operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 & 2 \\ 1 & 7 & 3 & 9 \\ 2 & 3 & 0 & 1 \\ 2 & 1 & 1 & 7\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}-2{C}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 & 2 \\ -5 & 7 & 3 & 9 \\ 2 & 3 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 7\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{2}:={C}_{2}-{C}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 & 2 \\ -5 & 4 & 3 & 9 \\ 2 & 3 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 7\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{4}:={C}_{4}-7{C}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 & 2 \\ -5 & 4 & 3 & -12 \\ 2 & 3 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =B.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding elementary column operations are

$\,$ ${C}_{1}:={C}_{1}-2{C}_{3}\,$ and $\,{C}_{4}:={C}_{4}-7{C}_{3}.$

$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $B$ above. By applying three matrix elementary column operations 

- ${C}_{1}:=…$
- ${C}_{2}:={C}_{2}-{C}_{3}$
- ${C}_{4}:=…$

each of the form ${C}_{i}:={C}_{i}+k{C}_{3},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the missing elementary column operations?
content.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries to the left and to the right of ${a}_{43}=1$ equal to $0.$

after.name: Question 17
after.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 2 & 7 \\ 1 & -7 & -4 & -6 \\ -1 & 3 & 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 7 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}7 & -6 & 2 & 3 \\ -3 & 5 & -4 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 4 & 1 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $B$ above. By applying three matrix elementary column operations 

- ${C}_{1}:={C}_{1}+{C}_{3}$
- ${C}_{2}:=…$
- ${C}_{4}:=…$

each of the form ${C}_{i}:={C}_{i}+k{C}_{3},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the missing elementary column operations?
after.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries to the left and to the right of ${a}_{33}=1$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary column operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 2 & 7 \\ 1 & -7 & -4 & -6 \\ -1 & 3 & 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 7 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}+{C}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}7 & 0 & 2 & 7 \\ -3 & -7 & -4 & -6 \\ 0 & 3 & 1 & 2 \\ 4 & 7 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{2}:={C}_{2}-3{C}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}7 & -6 & 2 & 7 \\ -3 & 5 & -4 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 4 & 1 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{4}:={C}_{4}-2{C}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}7 & -6 & 2 & 3 \\ -3 & 5 & -4 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 4 & 1 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding elementary column operations are

$\,$ ${C}_{2}:={C}_{2}-3{C}_{3}\,$ and $\,{C}_{4}:={C}_{4}-2{C}_{3}.$

content.knowledge_point: Using Column Operations to Create a Row of Zeros in a 4x4 Matrix
content.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 2 & 7 \\ 1 & -7 & -4 & -6 \\ -1 & 3 & 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 7 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}7 & -6 & 2 & 3 \\ -3 & 5 & -4 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 4 & 1 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $B$ above. By applying three matrix elementary column operations 

- ${C}_{1}:={C}_{1}+{C}_{3}$
- ${C}_{2}:=…$
- ${C}_{4}:=…$

each of the form ${C}_{i}:={C}_{i}+k{C}_{3},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the missing elementary column operations?
content.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries to the left and to the right of ${a}_{33}=1$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary column operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 2 & 7 \\ 1 & -7 & -4 & -6 \\ -1 & 3 & 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 7 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}+{C}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}7 & 0 & 2 & 7 \\ -3 & -7 & -4 & -6 \\ 0 & 3 & 1 & 2 \\ 4 & 7 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{2}:={C}_{2}-3{C}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}7 & -6 & 2 & 7 \\ -3 & 5 & -4 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 4 & 1 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{4}:={C}_{4}-2{C}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}7 & -6 & 2 & 3 \\ -3 & 5 & -4 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 4 & 1 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding elementary column operations are

$\,$ ${C}_{2}:={C}_{2}-3{C}_{3}\,$ and $\,{C}_{4}:={C}_{4}-2{C}_{3}.$

after.name: Question 18
after.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}7 & 5 & 6 & -9 \\ 6 & 4 & 2 & -6 \\ -7 & 2 & -3 & 6 \\ 5 & 6 & 1 & 8\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-11 & -7 & 6 & 9 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & 8 & -3 & -3 \\ 2 & 4 & 1 & 11\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $B$ above. By applying three matrix elementary column operations 

- ${C}_{1}:={C}_{1}-3{C}_{3}$
- ${C}_{2}:=…$
- ${C}_{4}:=…$

each of the form ${C}_{i}:={C}_{i}+k{C}_{3},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the missing elementary column operations?
after.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries to the left and to the right of ${a}_{23}=2$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary column operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}7 & 5 & 6 & -9 \\ 6 & 4 & 2 & -6 \\ -7 & 2 & -3 & 6 \\ 5 & 6 & 1 & 8\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}-3{C}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-11 & 5 & 6 & -9 \\ 0 & 4 & 2 & -6 \\ 2 & 2 & -3 & 6 \\ 2 & 6 & 1 & 8\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{2}:={C}_{2}-2{C}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-11 & -7 & 6 & -9 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & -6 \\ 2 & 8 & -3 & 6 \\ 2 & 4 & 1 & 8\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{4}:={C}_{4}+3{C}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-11 & -7 & 6 & 9 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & 8 & -3 & -3 \\ 2 & 4 & 1 & 11\end{aligned}] \\  & =B.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding elementary column operations are

$\,$ ${C}_{2}:={C}_{2}-2{C}_{3}\,$ and $\,{C}_{4}:={C}_{4}+3{C}_{3}.$

Consider the matrices A and B above. By applying three matrix elementary column operations

  1. C1:=C1−3C3
  2. C2:=…
  3. C4:=…
each of the form Ci:=Ci+kC3, the matrix A can be transformed into the matrix B. What are the missing elementary column operations?

a
C2:=C2−3C3 and C4:=C4+2C3
b
C2:=C2−2C3 and C4:=C4−3C3
c
C2:=C2+2C3 and C4:=C4+3C3

Submit

EXPLANATION

To transform A into B, we need to make entries to the left and to the right of a23=2 equal to 0.

To do this, we can apply the following elementary column operations:

A=[756−9642−6−72−365618]C1:=C1−3C3∼[−1156−9042−622−362618]C2:=C2−2C3∼[−11−76−9002−628−362418]C4:=C4+3C3∼[−11−769002028−3−324111]=B.

Therefore, the corresponding elementary column operations are

C2:=C2−2C3 and C4:=C4+3C3.

content.knowledge_point: Using Column Operations to Create a Row of Zeros in a 4x4 Matrix
content.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}7 & 5 & 6 & -9 \\ 6 & 4 & 2 & -6 \\ -7 & 2 & -3 & 6 \\ 5 & 6 & 1 & 8\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-11 & -7 & 6 & 9 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & 8 & -3 & -3 \\ 2 & 4 & 1 & 11\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $B$ above. By applying three matrix elementary column operations 

- ${C}_{1}:={C}_{1}-3{C}_{3}$
- ${C}_{2}:=…$
- ${C}_{4}:=…$

each of the form ${C}_{i}:={C}_{i}+k{C}_{3},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the missing elementary column operations?
content.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries to the left and to the right of ${a}_{23}=2$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary column operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}7 & 5 & 6 & -9 \\ 6 & 4 & 2 & -6 \\ -7 & 2 & -3 & 6 \\ 5 & 6 & 1 & 8\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}-3{C}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-11 & 5 & 6 & -9 \\ 0 & 4 & 2 & -6 \\ 2 & 2 & -3 & 6 \\ 2 & 6 & 1 & 8\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{2}:={C}_{2}-2{C}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-11 & -7 & 6 & -9 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & -6 \\ 2 & 8 & -3 & 6 \\ 2 & 4 & 1 & 8\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{4}:={C}_{4}+3{C}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-11 & -7 & 6 & 9 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & 8 & -3 & -3 \\ 2 & 4 & 1 & 11\end{aligned}] \\  & =B.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding elementary column operations are

$\,$ ${C}_{2}:={C}_{2}-2{C}_{3}\,$ and $\,{C}_{4}:={C}_{4}+3{C}_{3}.$

after.name: Question 19
after.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 4 & -2 & 8 \\ -6 & 9 & -3 & 7 \\ 4 & 2 & 1 & -8 \\ 5 & 4 & 3 & 3\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & -3 & -5 \\ 2 & 4 & 1 & -4 \\ -1 & 10 & 3 & 15\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $B$ above. By applying three matrix elementary column operations 

- ${C}_{1}:=…$
- ${C}_{2}:={C}_{2}+2{C}_{3}$
- ${C}_{4}:=…$

each of the form ${C}_{i}:={C}_{i}+k{C}_{3},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the missing elementary column operations?
after.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries to the left and to the right of ${a}_{13}=-2$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary column operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-4 & 4 & -2 & 8 \\ -6 & 9 & -3 & 7 \\ 4 & 2 & 1 & -8 \\ 5 & 4 & 3 & 3\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}-2{C}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & 4 & -2 & 8 \\ 0 & 9 & -3 & 7 \\ 2 & 2 & 1 & -8 \\ -1 & 4 & 3 & 3\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{2}:={C}_{2}+2{C}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & -2 & 8 \\ 0 & 3 & -3 & 7 \\ 2 & 4 & 1 & -8 \\ -1 & 10 & 3 & 3\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{4}:={C}_{4}+4{C}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & -3 & -5 \\ 2 & 4 & 1 & -4 \\ -1 & 10 & 3 & 15\end{aligned}] \\  & =B.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding elementary column operations are

$\,$ ${C}_{1}:={C}_{1}-2{C}_{3}\,$ and $\,{C}_{4}:={C}_{4}+4{C}_{3}.$

content.knowledge_point: Using Column Operations to Create a Row of Zeros in a 4x4 Matrix
content.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 4 & -2 & 8 \\ -6 & 9 & -3 & 7 \\ 4 & 2 & 1 & -8 \\ 5 & 4 & 3 & 3\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & -3 & -5 \\ 2 & 4 & 1 & -4 \\ -1 & 10 & 3 & 15\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $B$ above. By applying three matrix elementary column operations 

- ${C}_{1}:=…$
- ${C}_{2}:={C}_{2}+2{C}_{3}$
- ${C}_{4}:=…$

each of the form ${C}_{i}:={C}_{i}+k{C}_{3},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the missing elementary column operations?
content.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries to the left and to the right of ${a}_{13}=-2$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary column operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-4 & 4 & -2 & 8 \\ -6 & 9 & -3 & 7 \\ 4 & 2 & 1 & -8 \\ 5 & 4 & 3 & 3\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}-2{C}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & 4 & -2 & 8 \\ 0 & 9 & -3 & 7 \\ 2 & 2 & 1 & -8 \\ -1 & 4 & 3 & 3\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{2}:={C}_{2}+2{C}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & -2 & 8 \\ 0 & 3 & -3 & 7 \\ 2 & 4 & 1 & -8 \\ -1 & 10 & 3 & 3\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{4}:={C}_{4}+4{C}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & -3 & -5 \\ 2 & 4 & 1 & -4 \\ -1 & 10 & 3 & 15\end{aligned}] \\  & =B.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding elementary column operations are

$\,$ ${C}_{1}:={C}_{1}-2{C}_{3}\,$ and $\,{C}_{4}:={C}_{4}+4{C}_{3}.$

after.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 7 & 7 \\ -7 & -4 & 2 & -1 \\ 4 & 1 & 3 & 2 \\ 1 & 5 & 1 & 8\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-15 & 4 & -5 & -1 \\ 9 & -4 & 14 & 7 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ -19 & 5 & -14 & -2\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $B$ above. By applying three matrix elementary column operations 

- ${C}_{1}:=…$
- ${C}_{3}:={C}_{3}-3{C}_{2}$
- ${C}_{4}:=…$

each of the form ${C}_{i}:={C}_{i}+k{C}_{2},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the missing elementary column operations?
after.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries to the left and to the right of ${a}_{32}=1$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary column operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 7 & 7 \\ 7 & -4 & 2 & -1 \\ 4 & 1 & 3 & 2 \\ 1 & 5 & 1 & 8\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}-4{C}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-15 & 4 & 7 & 7 \\ 9 & -4 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & 2 \\ -19 & 5 & 1 & 8\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{3}:={C}_{3}-3{C}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-15 & 4 & -5 & 7 \\ 9 & -4 & 14 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 2 \\ -19 & 5 & -14 & 8\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{4}:={C}_{4}-2{C}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-15 & 4 & -5 & -1 \\ 9 & -4 & 14 & 7 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ -19 & 5 & -14 & -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =B.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding elementary column operations are

$\,$ ${C}_{1}:={C}_{1}-4{C}_{2}\,$ and $\,{C}_{4}:={C}_{4}-2{C}_{2}.$

Consider the matrices A and B above. By applying three matrix elementary column operations

  1. C1:=…
  2. C3:=C3−3C2
  3. C4:=…
each of the form Ci:=Ci+kC2, the matrix A can be transformed into the matrix B. What are the missing elementary column operations?

a
C1:=C1−4C2 and C4:=C4−2C2
b
C1:=C1−2C2 and C4:=C4−4C2
c
C1:=C1−4C2 and C4:=C4+2C2
d
C1:=C1+2C2 and C4:=C4+4C2
e
C1:=C1+4C2 and C4:=C4+2C2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

content.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 7 & 7 \\ -7 & -4 & 2 & -1 \\ 4 & 1 & 3 & 2 \\ 1 & 5 & 1 & 8\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-15 & 4 & -5 & -1 \\ 9 & -4 & 14 & 7 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ -19 & 5 & -14 & -2\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $B$ above. By applying three matrix elementary column operations 

- ${C}_{1}:=…$
- ${C}_{3}:={C}_{3}-3{C}_{2}$
- ${C}_{4}:=…$

each of the form ${C}_{i}:={C}_{i}+k{C}_{2},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the missing elementary column operations?
content.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries to the left and to the right of ${a}_{32}=1$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary column operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 7 & 7 \\ 7 & -4 & 2 & -1 \\ 4 & 1 & 3 & 2 \\ 1 & 5 & 1 & 8\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}-4{C}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-15 & 4 & 7 & 7 \\ 9 & -4 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & 2 \\ -19 & 5 & 1 & 8\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{3}:={C}_{3}-3{C}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-15 & 4 & -5 & 7 \\ 9 & -4 & 14 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 2 \\ -19 & 5 & -14 & 8\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{4}:={C}_{4}-2{C}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-15 & 4 & -5 & -1 \\ 9 & -4 & 14 & 7 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ -19 & 5 & -14 & -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =B.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding elementary column operations are

$\,$ ${C}_{1}:={C}_{1}-4{C}_{2}\,$ and $\,{C}_{4}:={C}_{4}-2{C}_{2}.$
